content:
# Sirach 35 — Disagreement Log

**Chapter:** SIR 035 | **Agents:** EMET, LOGOS, PNEUMA | **Total Disagreements:** 14

---

## Disagreement 1 — v.1: law-keeping as sacrifice (structural)

- **EMET:** "Whoever keeps the law multiplies offerings"
- **LOGOS:** "Keeping the law is worth many offerings"
- **PNEUMA:** "Living by God's instruction is itself an act of worship — it's worth more than many sacrifices"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** EMET's participial structure ("Whoever keeps") is more consistent with the rest of the chapter's paired sayings; PNEUMA's expansion adds commentary not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 2 — v.2: "shows gratitude" vs. "returns a kindness"

- **EMET:** "Whoever shows gratitude offers fine flour"
- **LOGOS:** "Returning a kindness is like presenting an offering of fine flour"
- **PNEUMA:** "Showing gratitude is like bringing a grain offering"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Whoever returns a kindness offers fine flour" — ἀνταποδίδων χάριν means "returning favor/kindness," which implies reciprocal social relationship; EMET's "shows gratitude" is slightly weaker.

---

## Disagreement 3 — v.3: "refrain from evil" vs. "turn away from evil"

- **EMET:** "To refrain from evil is pleasing to the Lord"
- **LOGOS:** "To refrain from wickedness is pleasing to the Lord"
- **PNEUMA:** "Turning away from evil pleases the Lord"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "To refrain from evil" — "wickedness" (LOGOS) over-specifies; "refrain" captures the ongoing discipline implied.

---

## Disagreement 4 — v.3b: "atonement" (all agree on word, differ on phrasing)

- All three use "atonement" but differ in structure.
- **EMET:** "to refrain from unrighteousness is an atonement"
- **LOGOS:** "to abstain from injustice is a means of atonement"
- **PNEUMA:** "turning away from wrongdoing makes atonement for sin"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "to abstain from injustice is an atonement" — LOGOS's verb "abstain" is more pointed than "refrain"; PNEUMA adds "for sin" not in the text.

---

## Disagreement 5 — v.5: "enriches the altar" — all agree; minor word order

- **EMET/LOGOS/PNEUMA:** All render "enriches the altar" similarly.
- **Minor diff:** "pleasing odor" (EMET) vs. "pleasing aroma" (LOGOS/PNEUMA).
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "pleasing aroma" — more natural modern English; "odor" has a slightly negative connotation in current usage.

---

## Disagreement 6 — v.7: "generously" placement

- **EMET:** "Honor the Lord generously"
- **LOGOS:** "Honor the Lord with generosity"
- **PNEUMA:** "Give generously to honor the Lord"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "Honor the Lord with generosity" — "with generosity" is more dignified than the adverb; PNEUMA restructures too freely.

---

## Disagreement 7 — v.9: "as he has given to you" — all agree; minor variation

- **EMET:** "Give to the Most High as he has given to you, generously, according to your means"
- **LOGOS:** "Give to the Most High as he has given you — generously, and according to your means"
- **PNEUMA:** "Give back to the Most High in proportion to what he has given you"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** LOGOS's version with the dash is most readable; "as he has given you" is slightly more natural than "as he has given to you."

---

## Disagreement 8 — v.11: "partiality" vs. "favoritism"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "no partiality"
- **PNEUMA:** "plays no favorites"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "no partiality" — the technical term προσωπολημψία (prosōpolēmpsia, literally "receiving of face") is the root of the NT's πρόσωπον formula; "partiality" is the standard English rendering of this theological concept.

---

## Disagreement 9 — v.12: "show partiality against a poor man" vs. "show no bias against the poor"

- **EMET:** "He will not show partiality against a poor man"
- **LOGOS:** "He does not show partiality against the poor"
- **PNEUMA:** "He shows no bias against the poor"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "will not show partiality against the poor" — present tense (LOGOS/PNEUMA) is defensible but future (EMET) may be part of the eschatological sequence; "partiality" is kept for consistency with v. 11.

---

## Disagreement 10 — v.13: "fatherless" vs. "orphan"

- **EMET:** "the fatherless"
- **LOGOS/PNEUMA:** "the orphan"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "the orphan" — ὀρφανοῦ; "orphan" is the more precise rendering and the standard wisdom-literature term.

---

## Disagreement 11 — v.16: "pierces the clouds" vs. "breaks through the clouds"

- **EMET/LOGOS:** "pierces the clouds"
- **PNEUMA:** "breaks through the clouds"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "pierces the clouds" — διακόπτει implies a sharp piercing action; "breaks through" is slightly too forceful and general.

---

## Disagreement 12 — v.17: divine action — "slow to act" vs. "patient"

- **EMET:** "nor will he be slow to act on their behalf"
- **LOGOS:** "nor will he be patient with them"
- **PNEUMA:** "he won't keep holding back"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "nor will he be slow on their behalf" — LOGOS's "patient with them" is ambiguous (patient with whom — the oppressors or the oppressed?); EMET's direction ("on their behalf") clarifies.

---

## Disagreement 13 — v.18: "crushes the loins" vs. "breaks the power"

- **EMET:** "until he crushes the loins of the merciless"
- **LOGOS:** "until he breaks the loins of the merciless"
- **PNEUMA:** "until he has broken the power of the pitiless"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "until he crushes the loins of the merciless" — the body-part imagery (ὀσφύν) is deliberately physical and should be preserved; PNEUMA's abstraction to "power" loses the visceral force.

---

## Disagreement 14 — v.20: rain simile

- **EMET:** "like rain clouds in time of drought"
- **LOGOS:** "as rain clouds during a drought"
- **PNEUMA:** "as welcome as rain in a drought"
- **Resolution (SOPHIA):** "as rain clouds in a time of drought" — "clouds" (EMET/LOGOS) preserves the anticipatory element: the clouds appear before the rain, i.e., mercy appears in the midst of trouble, not after it resolves.
